# Problem

`implement.py parent` / `implement.py drive` fail closed **before any session is
spawned** when the repository already holds ambient uncommitted work in the main
checkout or in other items' registered worktrees.
`_child_main_checkout_violation()` attributes that pre-existing dirt to a
never-spawned child whose own worktree is clean (zero commits ahead of `dev`),
because its "any other change surface holds changes" condition has no time
component. The only current exemption is the spawn-failure record, which exists
only after the driver has attempted a spawn and the session died
(SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G) — it cannot apply to a child that will be spawned by the
very same `phase_parent` call.

Reproduction (2026-11-17, `llm` epic `LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY`): a dirty main
checkout plus four dirty sibling worktrees plus a startable child with an
existing clean worktree ⇒ `drive` spawns **0** sessions and reports every dirty
surface as the child's stray write.

# User story

As an operator driving an epic, I want `implement.py drive <epic>` to start the
next startable child even when the repository already holds unrelated
uncommitted work, so that a long-lived checkout with several items in flight
does not make every epic undriveable.

# Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test builds the incident shape over real git sandboxes (`shared.git_sandbox`): ≥1 dirty tracked path in the main checkout, ≥1 dirty registered sibling worktree, and a startable (`open`) child with an existing clean worktree holding zero commits ahead of `dev`; `phase_parent` reports the child startable (`next_child` set, implementation action) with `placement_violation` not True and `success` True.
- A regression test asserts `phase_drive` spawns the next startable child in that scenario through an injected fake `spawn_session` (no real Pi session), and its report does not name any unrelated sibling worktree as an offender.
- A regression test asserts the genuine case still fails closed: a child whose session baseline predates the write and which writes only into the main checkout — or only into another item's linked worktree — is still reported as `placement_violation: True` even when other pre-existing dirt is present.
- Existing sibling-stray detection tests in `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` are updated to establish a session baseline before the injected write, and all continue to pass.
- The regression tests are written first (TDD) and land green. `implement.py finish` refuses a red tree, so they ship in the same commit as the fix children (mirroring SA-0MWGZ8E7C001X2HA / SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G).
- Full suite green at the dev-push gate (parent AC5) — the new regression tests and the existing suite pass together.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — incident reproduction, drive-spawn assertion, genuine-stray preservation.

# Tests

1. Never-spawned child + dirty main checkout + dirty sibling worktrees ⇒ `phase_parent` reports startable, no violation (parent AC1).
2. `phase_drive` in that scenario spawns exactly one child session via the fake spawner and names no sibling as an offender (parent AC3).
3. Session-baselined child writes only into the main checkout ⇒ still a placement violation (parent AC2).
4. Session-baselined child writes only into a sibling worktree ⇒ still a placement violation (parent AC2).

# Impact

A driver can start the next child of an epic on a checkout that already holds other items' uncommitted work, instead of every epic becoming undriveable until that dirt is cleaned.

# Downtime workers commit directly to dev in the main checkout, breaking the pushed-tip invariant

## Problem statement

Twice during epic SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1 the main checkout's `dev` carried **unpushed commits made directly in the main checkout** (not through a worktree `finish`), which made `implement.py start` refuse every new worktree with `Refusing to create a worktree from local dev: it is not a known pushed tip`. Recovery required publishing the foreign commits by hand, and the pre-push full-suite gate then `gate-refused` because the main checkout was dirty with a zero-content mode change (`100644 → 100755` on `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`).

The two observed commits were:

- `57768e2fe3` — `fix(machine-hygiene): remove shebang from config.py module (EXE001)` (no work-item id in the subject)
- `981af4d849` — `fix: Wrap implicit string concatenation in persist_audit.py (SA-0MWDKRD8G008Z164)` — landed by the herdr downtime worker for an item still `open`

## Root-cause verification (producer correction, 2026-11-18)

The producer's position — **the fix belongs in the skill layer, not the herdr dispatcher** — is correct on the substance, with one precision worth recording:

- The dispatcher is **not the committer**: `buildDowntimePaneArgs` only supplies `--cwd <main checkout root>`; it never runs `git commit`.
- The two observed commits are **ad-hoc agent commits**, not skill-helper commits. Both are authored `Sorra the Orc` and neither message is produced by any skill code path. The commit helpers that *can* commit are `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (message `audit: remediate ruff false positives (per-file-ignores)`) and `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` / `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (message `Auto-fix: <linter> applied fixes`).
- So the skill layer owns **both** the direct-commit helpers and the guardrails that should have stopped the ad-hoc commit. The dispatcher's `--cwd` is a contributing factor, not the defect.

Consequence for scope: option A (SorraAgents-only) is right, and AC3's **pre-commit hook** is the piece that catches ad-hoc agent commits — hardening the skill helpers alone would not have prevented either incident.

## Users

- **Herdr downtime dispatcher / downtime worker** — spawns `pi` panes with `--cwd <main checkout root>` and dispatches the `plan`, `intake`, `audit`, `implement` and `risk-effort` skills; a dispatched session that commits in that cwd poisons the shared `dev` ref for every other session.
- **Any implement session starting a worktree** — is blocked until the foreign commits are reconciled, regardless of which project or item it belongs to.
- **Producer / operator** — must currently reconcile by hand (inspect, verify, push or reset) with no attribution of which work item owns each foreign commit.

Example user stories:

- As an implement session, when I run `implement.py start`, I want a worktree created without first having to reconcile someone else's unpushed commits, so my work is never blocked by another session's shortcut.
- As a producer, when `start` refuses because `dev` is not a pushed tip, I want the refusal to name the work item(s) owning the unpushed commits, so reconciliation is one step instead of a manual log trawl.
- As the downtime worker, I want a dispatched session either to work in a worktree or to push what it commits before releasing the item, so the pushed-tip invariant is never broken by automation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The committing skills (`audit` `_commit_config_remediation`; `code-review` and `code_review` `_commit_changes`) either work in a worktree, refuse to commit on `dev` in the main checkout, or push what they commit before releasing the item.
- `start`'s refusal names the owning work items of the unpushed commits (subject scan) so reconciliation is one step.
- A `.githooks/pre-commit` hook refuses a commit on `dev` in the main checkout at commit time (zero-width window — the commit is never created), with an explicit operator override for deliberate hot-fixes, and a `git_sandbox` test proves it fires in the main checkout and does not fire in a worktree or on a feature branch.
- A `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` helper lists the `origin/dev..dev` commits with their owning work items and offers push (default) or reset, and is documented in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

One direct-on-dev commit from any session blocks worktree creation for every implement session in the repository until `dev` is reconciled; the higher the fan-out, the more often this recurs.

## Constraints

- **Worktree isolation.** SorraAgents implementation must happen in the worktree created by `implement.py start`; `finish` fails closed on writes outside it. The chosen scope (A) keeps every change inside a SorraAgents worktree.
- **Pushed-tip invariant.** `_resolve_start_base` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) deliberately refuses to branch from a local `dev` that is not a known pushed tip; that refusal must stay (it is the invariant, not the bug).
- **Fail-open on an unreachable remote.** A failed `git fetch` still branches from local `dev` (documented offline fallback) — the guard must not make offline work impossible.
- **No new blocking of legitimate finishes.** The post-push fast-forward of the main checkout's `dev` (SA-0MWFKDH78002T2CR) is a fast-forward, not a commit, so the pre-commit hook must not fire on it. `wl sync` commits on `refs/worklog/data`, not `dev`, so it is also unaffected.
- **Operator override.** A deliberate operator hot-fix on `dev` in the main checkout must remain possible via an explicit opt-in (e.g. `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1`), so the hook does not become an absolute prohibition.
- **UK English** in all written output.

## Existing state

- **The dispatcher runs panes in the main checkout.** `buildDowntimePaneArgs` forwards `--cwd <worklog root>` and `spawnAgentPane`/`spawnDowntimePane` spawn the pane there (`packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `…/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`, `…/index.ts`). The dispatcher's skill kinds are `plan | intake | audit | implement | risk-effort`.
- **Skills that commit in their cwd.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈ line 14222) stages the config file and runs `git commit` **locally, no push**. `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈ line 425) and a duplicate `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈ line 641) run `git add .` + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: …"`.
- **`start` already refuses, but opaquely.** `_resolve_start_base` (`implement.py` ≈ line 8021) detects `local_dev_not_a_pushed_tip` and `phase_start` posts a comment (≈ line 12090) naming only the two tips and a three-step manual remedy — no attribution of the foreign commits to work items.
- **The pushed-tip guarantees are documented.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (≈ line 2638) describes the three cooperating guarantees (pre-push deferral, post-push fast-forward, ancestry assertion) and the `_resolve_start_base` refusal.
- **A placement guard exists.** `implement.py` has implementation-placement gates (`SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2`) and a read-only pre-claim foreign-mutation check of the main checkout, but they only cover sessions that go through the implement skill.
- **A dirty-checkout check exists.** `scripts/hygiene_check.sh::check_dirty_checkout` warns on a dirty main checkout, but it does not detect **committed-but-unpushed** `dev` commits.
- **A live-repo mutation guard exists.** `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` plus `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` fail a test run that mutates a live ref — a candidate precedent for AC3's guard.
- **No pre-commit hook exists.** `.githooks/` ships `pre-push`, `pre-push.v2`, `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` and `worklog-post-pull`; `core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, so a new executable `.githooks/pre-commit` is picked up automatically. `scripts/install_pi.sh` wires and refreshes the pre-push hook idempotently — the pre-commit hook needs the same treatment.

## Desired change

1. **Close the direct-commit path (skill side).** Harden `audit`'s and `code-review`/`code_review`'s commit helpers so they refuse (or redirect to a worktree, or push before release) when they would commit on `dev` in the main checkout.
2. **Attribute the refusal.** Parse the work-item ids out of the subjects of `origin/dev..dev` and include them in the `start` refusal message and its work-item comment, so reconciliation is one step.
3. **Add the immediate guard.** Add `.githooks/pre-commit` that refuses a commit on `dev` in the main checkout (with an operator override), wire it into `scripts/install_pi.sh`, and prove it with a `git_sandbox` test.
4. **Add the reconciliation helper.** Add `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` (list with owning items; push default, reset opt-in) and document it in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
5. **Record the dispatcher follow-up.** A ContentCreator/herdr dispatcher change (spawn in a worktree) is out of scope here and recorded as a linked follow-up — its worklog is not initialised (0-byte DB), mirroring the SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC cross-repo precedent.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_start_base` (≈ 8021) and the `phase_start` refusal comment (≈ 12090): add the unpushed-commit subject scan and name the owning work items.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_commit_config_remediation` (≈ 14222): refuse/redirect/push when committing on `dev` in the main checkout.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `_commit_changes` (≈ 425) and `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` (≈ 641): same guard (and reconcile the duplicate directory).
- `.githooks/pre-commit` — new pre-commit hook (main-checkout + `dev` detection, operator override).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — install/refresh the pre-commit hook idempotently, beside the existing pre-push wiring.
- `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` — new reconciliation helper (list + push/reset).
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — `check_dirty_checkout` (≈ 179): optionally extend to unpushed-`dev` detection.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — reconciliation helper documentation (≈ 2638 section).
- `tests/` (e.g. `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py`) — `git_sandbox` proofs for the hook and the `start` attribution.
- `packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `…/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`, `…/index.ts` (ContentCreator) — **out of scope**, linked follow-up only.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** — finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly (completed). Same pushed-tip invariant family.
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** — Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit (completed). Establishes that `finish` pushes from the checkout holding the commit.
- **SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2** — Enforce git worktree usage for all implementation work (completed). Establishes the worktree requirement and the placement gate that this item extends to non-implement sessions.
- **SA-0MWFKDH78002T2CR** — deferred post-push fast-forward (referenced by the pushed-tip docs).
- **SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC** — cross-repo hand-off precedent (herdr emitter filed in SorraAgents).
- Parent epic: **SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1** (discovered from).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Ad-hoc-commit risk (medium).** The observed incidents were ad-hoc agent commits, not skill-helper commits, so the skill-helper hardening alone is insufficient — AC3's pre-commit hook is the necessary backstop. Both must land.
- **Guard false-positive risk (medium).** The pre-commit hook must not fire on the post-push fast-forward (not a commit), on `wl sync` (commits on `refs/worklog/data`), or in a worktree/feature branch. A `git_sandbox` test must pin each case.
- **Duplicate-directory risk (medium).** `skill/code-review/` and `skill/code_review/` both exist and both commit; only `code-review` has a `SKILL.md`. Fixing one and not the other would leave a live direct-commit path.
- **Operator hot-fix risk (medium).** An absolute prohibition on committing on `dev` in the main checkout would block legitimate operator hot-fixes; the explicit override keeps that path open.
- **Scope-creep risk (medium).** The dispatcher change (spawn in a worktree) is a ContentCreator concern; record it as a linked follow-up, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the "bounded window" for AC3 is **zero-width** — the pre-commit hook refuses the commit before it exists.
- **Assumption:** the reconciliation helper's default action is `push`; `reset --hard` requires explicit confirmation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Where does the fix live (scope split)?**
- Asked: The downtime dispatcher lives in ContentCreator (`packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/`), but this item is filed in SorraAgents and AC2/AC4 are SorraAgents-side.
- Answer (producer, 2026-11-18): "I don't think you are correct, I believe it's in the skill not the dispatcher. Correct me if I'm wrong. In the meantime do A." → **Option (a) SorraAgents-only.** Verification: the producer is correct — the dispatcher never commits; the observed commits are ad-hoc agent commits and the skill layer owns both the commit helpers and the guardrails. The dispatcher `--cwd` is a contributing factor only, recorded as a linked ContentCreator follow-up.

**Q2 — What form does the AC3 guard take, and what is the "bounded window"?**
- Asked: pre-commit hook vs suite test vs hygiene-check extension.
- Answer (producer, 2026-11-18): "A" → **pre-commit hook** (`.githooks/pre-commit`) refusing a commit on `dev` in the main checkout, plus a `git_sandbox` test. Bounded window = **zero-width** (commit never created). Operator override retained for deliberate hot-fixes.

**Q3 — What is the "unpushed-commit reconciliation helper"?**
- Asked: documentation only vs script + documentation.
- Answer (producer, 2026-11-18): "B" → **script + documentation**: `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` (list `origin/dev..dev` with owning work items; push default, reset opt-in) documented in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

*All questions answered; intake complete.*

As the implementer of the commit-time guard, I want a hermetic test that pins
exactly when `.githooks/pre-commit` must refuse and when it must stay silent, so

- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` is the precedent for a throw-away repo
  built from the committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` is the precedent for asserting the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` wiring block itself.
- The guard target is narrow: **`dev` in the main checkout**. A linked worktree,
  a feature branch, `git merge --ff-only` and a `wl sync` commit must all pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new hermetic module `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` builds a
  throw-away repository from the committed `.githooks/` with
  `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a bare local `origin` and a sandboxed `$HOME`; it
  never touches the real checkout, the real `$HOME` or the network.
- It asserts a commit on `dev` in the main checkout is **refused at commit time**:
  non-zero exit, `HEAD` unchanged, no new commit object, and the refusal message
  names the branch (`dev`), the main checkout path, the worktree requirement and
  the operator override.
- Zero-width proof: after the refused commit attempt the repository's commit
  count and `git rev-parse HEAD` are byte-identical to the pre-attempt values.
- It asserts the hook does **not** fire (exit 0, commit created) when:
  (a) the same commit runs inside a linked worktree (`git worktree add`);
  (b) the main checkout is on a feature branch;

  `wl sync`-style commit performed inside a temporary linked worktree

  new module passes once the hook item lands, and is red before it (the hook

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` builds once (Step 2), then pushes to `dev`. When the push
loses a race and is rejected non-fast-forward, `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
fetches `origin/dev`, rebases the feature branch, recomputes the commit hash
and retries the push — **without rebuilding the worktree**. The pre-push hook
then runs the full suite against the rebased tree, where `packages/shared/dist`
(gitignored, produced by the build) is stale with respect to the `dev` commits
the rebase just pulled in. The gate goes red for a condition that does not
exist in a built tree, and the item's work is stranded until a human rebuilds.

## Users

- **Dispatch agent (leaf `finish` / driven child)** — "When my push loses a
  race to a sibling push, I want the retry to gate a tree I actually built, so
  my item lands instead of failing on a `TypeError` that names a function my
  own change set never touched."
- **Producer / operator on duty** — "I want a red dev-push gate to always mean
  something real about the pushed change set, so I never spend an hour and a
  half hand-rebuilding a worktree to clear a false red."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a successful recovery rebase inside the push loop, `finish` builds the
   rebased worktree **before** the retry push reaches the full-suite gate. A
   test simulates a non-fast-forward rejection whose rebase introduces a new
   `packages/shared` export and asserts (a) the build ran between the rebase and
   the retry push, and (b) the recorded push verdict is green/pushed.
2. A stale-dist failure is never attributed to the item's own change set. A
   test asserts that a gate failure whose symptom is a stale shared build
   (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function` — a runtime error that the
   existing load-flake retry does not match) cannot be reported as a failure of
   the pushed change set: either the run rebuilds first, or it fails closed with
   a build/resolution diagnosis naming the stale `packages/shared/dist`.
3. A genuine red introduced by the rebased commit is still reported red. A test
   pins that the rebuild does not weaken the gate: when the rebased tree really
   fails the suite, the push is blocked and the item stays `open`.
4. `finish` on a worktree whose push is rejected once still lands the commit and
   writes the terminal `completed` / `in_review` transition (no manual
   intervention).
5. A rebuild that itself fails after the rebase fails **closed**: no push, an
   actionable comment naming the build failure and the worktree, and the item is
   reset to `open` (mirroring the existing Step 2 build-failure path) — an
   unbuilt tree is never gated.
6. No extra build is paid when no rebase happened: the normal (uncontended) push
   path keeps exactly one build per `finish`, and the changed-scope gate
   (Step 3) is never re-entered by the retry loop.
7. Tests for every behaviour above are added to the `skill/implement` suite and
   pass, and the new tests fail against the pre-change implementation (no
   vacuous green).
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A dispatch whose push races another push lands its work instead of spending an
hour and a half chasing a build-staleness false-red.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing single build entry point `run_build(cwd)` so the rebuild
  inherits the current behaviour (disk-backed `TMPDIR` injection, 300 s timeout,
  no-build-script no-op for Python-only repos) — no parallel build code path.
- The rebuild runs **inside** the push retry loop, after the rebase and before
  the retry `git_push_to_dev` call; the Step 3 changed-scope gate and the
  "at most one full-suite gate per finish" property (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) must
  survive.
- Never weaken the gate: a reproducible red on the rebuilt tree still blocks the
  push.
- Stay within the module's existing retry budget semantics
  (`DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`): a rebuild failure is a hard stop, not a
  retryable transport condition.
- Worktree-only changes; no behaviour change for the main checkout.

## Existing state

- `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:12262`)
  does: fetch `origin/dev` → `git rebase origin/dev` → capture the rewritten
  hash → `_assert_push_subject` → retry `git_push_to_dev`. There is no build
  step anywhere on this path.
- `run_build` (`implement.py:9324`) is the single build entry point; `phase_finish`
  Step 2 calls it once before tests (`implement.py:12763`).
- The pre-push gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) runs the full suite for `dev` pushes,
  bound to the pushed commit via `run_tests.py --gate-commit`, resolved by
  `resolve_gate_subject` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:3697`) — normally the
  worktree in place ("cheap in-place run"), so the suite executes against the
  worktree's filesystem including its `packages/shared/dist`.
- The verdict is tree-keyed (SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG) with change-set reuse
  (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC): a pure rebase is usually served from the pre-race
  verdict, so no suite runs. When the change set fingerprint **also** differs —
  e.g. the concurrently landed commit edited the same hub file the item edited
  (`packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` in the observed case) — the key misses,
  the suite really runs, and it runs on stale `dist`.
- Existing mitigation `_is_gate_load_flake` (`implement.py:6032`) retries once on
  suite *load* errors (`Cannot find package`, `Cannot find module`,
  `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). A stale-dist runtime `TypeError` **loads fine** and falls
  outside those patterns, and retrying the identical unbuilt tree could not help
  anyway.
- `packages/shared/dist` is gitignored and produced by `npm run build`, so it is
  invisible to the tree fingerprint: two trees with identical git content can
  carry different `dist` contents. That is precisely the mismatch this item is
  about.
- Evidence (2026-11-18, ContextHub epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9, child
  WL-0MWKY141H002LULI): two consecutive false reds in one session — attempt 1
  rebased in `508a1821e` (`isNotStarted`) → 17 × `TypeError: isNotStarted is not
  a function`; attempt 2 rebased in `ac2a2c48e` (`normalizeStartOn`) → multiple
  `TypeError: normalizeStartOn is not a function`. Both cleared with no source
  change: `git fetch origin dev && git rebase origin/dev && npm run build` →
  `finish` green. Direct proof of staleness: `grep -c normalizeStartOn
  packages/shared/dist/predicates.js` → `0` before the manual build, `2` after.

## Desired change

The item offers three mechanisms; research picks one as primary and one as a
cheap hardening, and records why the third cannot fix the defect alone.

**A — Rebuild after a recovery rebase (recommended, primary).** After the
successful `git rebase origin/dev` in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`, and
before the retry push, call `run_build(worktree_path)`. On failure, fail closed
(no retry push, failure comment naming the build stderr tail and the worktree,
item reset to `open`). Rationale: it makes the gate's subject and the build
consistent by construction, costs one build per rebase round (the rebase round
already costs a push attempt, and at most 5 rounds run), and needs no new
persistent state.

**B — Refuse to gate a tree newer than the last build (recommended hardening).**
Record the built tree SHA when the build succeeds (a `_set_finish_progress`
field / report field is enough — no new file format), and before a retry push
verify that `HEAD^{tree}` still matches it; when it does not, rebuild. This
generalises A to the other tree-changing paths that can precede a push (amend,
`git pull`, a rebase performed outside the recovery helper) at near-zero cost.
The fail-closed branch of the item's option 2 is therefore available as the
backstop without inventing a new abort source on the normal path.

**C — Rebuild-scoped cache key (rejected as a standalone fix).** The gate's key
is derived from the git tree (or the change-set patch), and `packages/shared/dist`
is gitignored, so a build-scoped key component could only be added by hashing a
build artifact into the key. That would invalidate verdicts for every unrelated
`finish` (every build produces a different `dist`), and it does not address the
actual defect: the suite *did* legitimately re-run, then failed on a stale
artifact. Keying cannot make an unbuilt tree built.

**Non-negotiable invariant (from the item):** whatever mechanism is implemented,
the push loop must never report a *source-level* test failure for a tree it did
not build.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  (~12262) gains the post-rebase rebuild (A) / built-tree check (B); the push
  loop in `phase_finish` (~13560–13660) surfaces the rebuild in
  `report["steps"]["push"]`; `run_build` (~9324) reused unchanged;
  `_set_finish_progress` (~759) carries the built-tree marker for B.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the existing
  non-fast-forward / load-flake harness (`_stubbed_finish`, `sandbox`) is the
  place for the AC1–AC5 tests.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — drop-in coverage for the
  recovery helper if the rebuild is asserted at helper level rather than through
  `phase_finish`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — the "A lost push race does not re-run
  the full suite" section (~2578) and the push-robustness list (~1715) need the
  post-rebase build documented alongside the change-set reuse they describe.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the false red is caused by a stale build artifact, not by a
  wrong `dev` merge. The evidence (`isNotStarted` / `normalizeStartOn` in source
  but absent from `dist`, cleared by `npm run build` alone) supports this; if a
  similar red survives a rebuild, it is a genuine regression and must stay red
  (AC3).
- **Risk — rebuild churn vs. the push-subject guard.** On game repos `npm run
  build` runs `engine:sync` first, which can advance the engine submodule and
  stage the pin/gitlink. `_assert_push_subject` refuses a push from a worktree
  with tracked uncommitted changes, so a churn-producing rebuild could turn a
  recoverable race into a `PushSubjectMismatchError`. Mitigation: snapshot the
  churn baseline before the post-rebase build (reusing `_build_churn_baseline`),
  attribute the churn as finish's own like Step 2 does, and fail closed with an
  actionable comment when the churn cannot be carried.
- **Risk — cost.** One extra build per rebase round (≤ `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT`
  = 5 rounds). Accepted: it is far cheaper than the observed false-red recovery,
  and it is not paid on the uncontended path (AC6).
- **Risk — masking.** A rebuild that *hides* a real failure would be worse than
  the bug. Mitigated by AC3's pin test and by keeping the gate's verdict
  untouched: the rebuild changes what the suite measures, never the pass/fail
  threshold.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Making the full-suite cache key build-aware
  (mechanism C), hardening the load-flake pattern list, or re-running the suite
  after every rebase are **out of scope**; each is either rejected above or worth
  its own item. Any such finding during implementation is recorded as a linked

## Goal

A recurring post-push verification refusal with `verdict=missing` (no full-suite cache entry for the pushed tree) is filed as a **critical `[test-failure]` item named "… — failing test"**, whose acceptance criteria no agent can satisfy, and every recurrence creates a *new* item because the triage dedupe only looks at critical items. Route such refusals as **gate/cache artefacts** and dedupe the signature **across priorities**.

## Root cause

1. **Mislabelling.** `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_post_push_failure_test_name()` falls back to `post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry` when no entry is `verdict=red`, and `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage()` files it through the triage helper exactly like a real regression. A cache miss therefore becomes a critical, agent-blocking "test failure" whose ACs ("the test … passes") cannot be met, and which only a human may close (false-positive rule in the runbook).
2. **Dedupe gap.** `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py::list_critical_issues()` queries `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure` only, so all three match heuristics are blind to an identical signature at any other priority. Evidence: the same signature already existed as `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` (commit `8169e29`, priority **high**) yet a second item, `VC-0MWOI6V8J000FHFL` (commit `af9370f`, critical), was created. The helper's documented "an existing matching critical `test-failure` item is enhanced instead of duplicated" contract consequently only holds among critical items.

## Producer decisions (2026-11-20)

- **Routing:** the fix lives in this repo (`SorraAgents`); the video_compiler item was a routing shell and was deleted after this item was filed.
- **Behaviour:** **keep the fail-closed refusal.** This item adds **no** self-heal and no finish-time suite runs; the cache-miss root cause remains with `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` (key the pre-push gate verdict on the pushed tree) and `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L` (cache key ignores worktree/env identity).
- **Duplicate:** `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` was closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Scope (test-first ordering)

1. **Tests first** (`skill/triage/tests/`, `skill/implement/tests/`):
   - cross-priority signature match: an identical signature on a `high`-priority existing item is matched, a comment is added, and no second item is created;
   - gate-artefact routing: a `verdict=missing` refusal produces a gate-artefact title/tag with agent-satisfiable ACs;
   - regression guard: `verdict=red` still names the failing test from suite output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
2. `check_or_create.py`: match across all priorities (and by signature/commit), keeping "enhance, never duplicate"; record the recurrence as a comment on the existing item.
3. `implement.py`: name and route a `verdict=missing` refusal as a gate/cache artefact — distinct title prefix, tag, and ACs an agent can satisfy. The refusal itself stays fail-closed.
4. Runbook: add a "Gate/cache artefacts" subsection beside "Environmental failure signatures" in `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`, including the remediation (`run_tests.py --scope full`, then re-run `finish`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A post-push `verdict=missing` refusal is filed with a gate-artefact title prefix and tag, never as `[test-failure] … — failing test`, and its acceptance criteria are satisfiable by an agent.
2. An identical failure signature matches regardless of the existing item's priority: a recurrence adds a comment to the existing item and creates no second item (regression test covers a `high`-priority existing item).
3. `verdict=red` routing is unchanged: a red entry still names the failing test from its output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
4. The triage runbook documents the gate/cache-artefact signature and its remediation.
5. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

A cache-miss refusal stops masquerading as a critical test failure, so agents are no longer blocked by an item nobody can close and operators see one tracker per signature instead of one per commit.

## Key Files

- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`
- `skill/triage/tests/`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/`

- `list_critical_issues()` in `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` (near line 51).

# Epic drive cannot spawn headless child sessions — `pi -p` fails model resolution

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MWMPAW9P002DGZF (face-off parity epic), while driving its children on 2026-11-20. Replaces the tce-the-rising report RISE-0MWOIAJZJ002QYUO, which was re-homed here because the fix belongs to this repository.

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive <parent>` spawns a fresh headless child session per child, but on this machine every child session dies at startup because its model cannot be resolved (`No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` / provider `finish_reason: error`). The driver then burns its entire infrastructure-retry budget (5 attempts, 2 s doubling to 30 s) before stopping the chain, so an epic cannot be advanced by `drive` at all.

## Users

- **Operator driving an epic** (`/skill:implement <epic>` or the herdr downtime worker): "I want `drive` to spawn child sessions that actually run, so an epic progresses without me opening one session per child."
- **Operator diagnosing a stalled drive:** "I want an immediate, actionable failure naming the unresolvable pattern and the available providers, instead of five identical retries and a vague stop."

## Impact

An epic can be driven to completion by `drive` again — children spawn on a real model, and a genuinely unresolvable model pattern fails in seconds with a message that says what to fix, rather than stalling the whole chain for minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `drive` resolves the child session's model to a concrete, available `provider/model` pair before spawning and passes it explicitly (`--provider`/`--model`), **and** pre-validates that resolved model against the available model catalogue, refusing to spawn when it cannot be resolved. A permanently-unresolvable pattern fails fast (no infrastructure retries consumed) with a message naming the pattern and the available providers.
- A regression test drives the spawn-argument / pre-spawn validation path with an unresolvable pattern and asserts the fast-fail message and that no infra retries are consumed; a resolvable pattern still produces a correct argv that explicitly names the resolved concrete model, pinned by test.
- A manual verification records a `drive` run on a two-child parent completing both children on a machine configured with the local proxy.
- Documentation (implement skill reference → drive failure recovery, and the spawn-failure classification section) records the fast-fail behaviour and how to set a concrete model for driven sessions.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing spawn-failure semantics from SA-0MWLDZBTF004LJFP: an *unknown* failure still hard-stops the chain; only a genuinely transient provider/credential failure may use the bounded infra budget.
- Do **not** duplicate the configuration-side fix. Removing the unservable `MunitoAI/*` glob from the tracked Pi config is owned by SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN; this item is the drive-side resilience that makes any such pattern fail fast and spawn a concrete model.
- Pi does not consume `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL` for its own model selection (they are exported to bash tools as session context), so relying on the child to "inherit the driver's resolved model" is not a valid fix — the model must be resolved and passed explicitly, and/or the child's own resolution validated before spawning.
- Scope-creep risk: do not attempt a general rewrite of Pi model resolution; confine changes to the drive spawner, the pre-spawn validation and the spawn-failure classifier. Record anything larger as a separate linked item.

## Existing state

- `_default_session_spawner` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` builds `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions` and passes **no** `--provider`/`--model` flag.
- `_child_session_env` removes only `PI_SESSION_ID`/`PI_SESSION_FILE`; it keeps `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL`, but Pi does not consume those for its own model selection, so the child re-resolves from `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (`defaultProvider`/`defaultModel`/`enabledModels`).
- The live `enabledModels` contains the glob `MunitoAI/*`, which matches nothing because `MUNITOAI_API_KEY` is absent; `pi` emits `Warning: No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` on every invocation, and the child can select a model that errors at request time (`Provider finish_reason: error`).
- `classify_spawn_failure` correctly labels this `infrastructure` and retries it up to the shared budget; it cannot recover from a pattern that will never resolve.
- Related features already shipped: SA-0MWLDZBTF004LJFP (bounded infra retry for spawn-time provider failures), SA-0MWLDZ8ZN0030T15 (spawn-failure classification tests), SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN (remove invalid/stale model ids and the `MunitoAI/*` glob from the tracked Pi config).

## Desired change

Make the drive child spawn deterministic about its model: resolve and pass a concrete available `provider/model`, pre-validate it against the catalogue, and if it cannot be resolved, fail fast with an actionable message naming the pattern and the available providers — instead of exhausting five retries.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_default_session_spawner` / `_pane_session_spawner` spawn argv, `_child_session_env`, `classify_spawn_failure`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — spawn-argument / pre-spawn validation regression tests
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — drive failure recovery and spawn-failure classification sections

## Related work

- **RISE-0MWOIAJZJ002QYUO** — the original tce-the-rising report (deleted; re-homed to this item).
- **RISE-0MWMRBRFR0094KR0** — Face-off beat parity matrix (VFX): the child whose spawn failed, reproducing the defect.
- **RISE-0MWMPAW9P002DGZF** — Face-Offs initiated by the adversaries should be identical: the parent epic whose `drive` run surfaced this.
- **RISE-0MWOIAXAG008HMK3** — drive's sibling-worktree guard fails closed on pre-existing dirt: a separate `drive` robustness defect.
- **SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN** — Remove invalid and stale model ids from the tracked Pi configuration: owns removing the unservable `MunitoAI/*` glob (config-side root cause). Not a duplicate — complementary.
- **SA-0MWLDZBTF004LJFP** — Bounded infra retry for spawn-time provider failures: the retry behaviour this item makes fail fast on a permanent pattern.
- **SA-0MWLDZ8ZN0030T15** — Tests for spawn-failure provider classification.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (work-item home / cross-repo dispatch):** Options were (A) keep in `RISE` with manual SorraAgents-checkout implementation; (B) re-home/re-file as a SorraAgents `SA-*` item; (C) file a SorraAgents child and link. **Answer (producer, this session): "recreate the item in ../SorraAgents and delete this one."** Accepted: option (B). This item is the recreation; the `RISE` item is deleted.
- **Q2 (fix approach):** Options were (A) explicit `--provider/--model`; (B) pre-validate the child's resolved model and fail fast; (C) both. **Answer (producer, this session): "as you recommend"** → option (C), both. The AC1 phrase "or omits the flag so the child inherits the driver's resolved model" has been removed because Pi does not consume `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL` for its own model selection.

- **SA-0MWM88J2D001HFMS** – Fix: session-baseline lifecycle across start/parent/drive (blocked)

# Audit code-quality scan resolves `--code-root` file scope against the launch cwd (cross-repo E902 ghosts block Phase 1)

**Discovered from:** WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 (Create a podcast for standups) — a cross-repo item tracked in the ContextHub worklog whose delivered code lives in the ContentCreator repository. Found during `/skill:audit` on 2026-11-21.

## Problem statement

When an audit is launched from the **worklog owner's** checkout with `--code-root <other repo>`, the code-quality scan builds a scope from repository-relative names but the linter subprocess runs in the **process cwd** (the launch checkout), so `ruff` cannot find the files and reports `E902 No such file or directory` — a *high* severity finding. High findings are blocking, so Phase 2 is skipped and the audit fails closed with `Ready to close: No` for work that is actually complete.

## Users

- **Producers running cross-repo audits** — a standup/podcast item tracked in one project while its code lives in another currently audits to a false "not ready" verdict: *"As a producer, I want a cross-repo audit to report the item's true state so I do not re-run it from a different directory to get a valid result."*
- **Agent sessions invoking `/skill:audit`** — must not spend a run (and a Phase 1 model call) on fabricated lint findings.
- **Maintainers of the audit skill** — need the cwd-dependence removed at the source rather than documented as a launch caveat.

## Observed evidence

Launch (from `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`):

```bash
audit_runner.py issue WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 \
  --code-root /home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator \
  --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog
```

Reported findings (all `high`, all fabricated, all `ruff`/`E902`):

| File | Line | Message |
|---|---|---|
| /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.pi/skills/wiki-podcast-script/scripts/convert_standup.py | 1 | No such file or directory (os error 2) |
| /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/rss_server.py | 1 | No such file or directory (os error 2) |
| /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/tests/test_standups_podcast_pipeline.py | 1 | No such file or directory (os error 2) |

All three files exist and lint cleanly in the code root (`ContentCreator`); none existed under the launch cwd (`ContextHub`). The `--code-root` mechanism itself worked: the log records `Warning: dropped 1 path(s) from the code-quality scope ... — linting 7 in-scope file(s) only`, and the report's `## Audit Scope` names both roots correctly. A re-run launched **from the code root** resolved the same scope correctly and produced zero code-quality findings — strong evidence that the defect is cwd-dependent, not item-dependent.

Logs: `~/.audit_debug/ContextHub/audit_run_WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8_20261121T213400.log` (bad run), `..._20261121T215624_rerun.log` (good run).

## Existing state (verified in this intake)

- `audit_runner._phase_fetch_and_cq` resolves the scope with `_resolve_code_quality_scope(..., project_root=per_audit_root)`, where `per_audit_root` **is** the code root when `--code-root` is set (`_phase_gate`, line ~13159). Git-derived evidence is already cwd-safe: `_cwd_aware_runner(git_root, runner)` prefixes `git -C <git_root>` whenever the code root differs from the launch root, so `_git_changed_files` is **not** the defect.
- `_resolve_code_quality_scope` returns **relative** paths (`_filter_code_quality_scope` keeps them "unchanged and in order" — SA-0MVPDTSRV0049KW2 AC5).
- `_filter_existing_paths(paths, project_root)` accepts a relative path when `(root / p).exists() **or** Path(path).exists()` — the second clause is an implicit **cwd-relative** stat against the launch root, so a same-named file in the launch checkout can keep a path that does not exist in the code root (the ghost source; SA-0MSXVXVUL0011JKX introduced the filter without this being cross-repo-safe).
- `run_code_quality(..., files=...)` → `run_linters_for_project(..., files=...)` → `_run_ruff_check(root, runner, files)` builds `["ruff", "check", *files, ...]` and calls `runner(cmd)` with **no `cwd`**, so relative paths resolve against the process cwd. `Runner` is typed `Callable[[Sequence[str]], CompletedProcess]` — it has no `cwd` keyword today.
- The live package is `skill/code_review/` (underscore); `skill/code-review/` is a stale, unsymlinked copy whose `run_code_quality` has **no** `files` parameter. Only `code_review` (underscore) is imported by the audit.

## Desired change

Make the code-quality scan's file resolution independent of the process cwd, and make the scope honest about what exists in the code root.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A cross-repo audit launched from a checkout other than `--code-root` produces **no** `E902` code-quality findings for files that exist in the code root; files that do not exist under the code root are dropped from the scope (never linted), and the scan either lints the correct files or reports the documented empty-scope skip reason.
- [ ] Linter path resolution is cwd-independent: with the process cwd differing from the code root, every path handed to the linter resolves to an existing file under the code root, and `_filter_existing_paths` no longer keeps a path merely because it exists relative to the process cwd.
- [ ] Regression tests pin the behaviour at both layers: scope resolution (`skill/audit/tests/`) — with `project_root` != process cwd the scope contains only code-root files, no cwd-relative survivors; linter invocation (`tests/`) — the argv handed to the runner resolves to existing files when the process cwd differs, and no `E902` finding is produced.
- [ ] Same-repo audits are unchanged: when the code root equals the launch root the resolved scope and linter argv are identical to pre-fix behaviour (pinned by an assertion in the new/extended tests).
- [ ] `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` states the cross-repo launch requirement accurately after the fix (launching from the code root remains safest, and `--code-root` alone no longer mis-resolves linter paths).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Cross-repo work items are no longer falsely failed by the audit: a standup/podcast item tracked in one project with code in another audits to its true verdict instead of being blocked by fabricated lint errors, so producers stop re-running audits from a different directory to get a valid result.

## Constraints

- **Read-only audits.** The fix must not introduce `--fix`, writes, or checkouts in the code repository.
- **No launch-cwd regression.** Items whose code lives in the launch/owning checkout must produce a byte-identical scope and linter argv.
- **Do not widen scope.** An empty or fully filtered scope must still skip the scan with `_CODE_QUALITY_SCOPE_EMPTY_REASON`; never fall back to a whole-repository lint.
- **Two call sites.** The Phase 1 scan and the remediation re-scan both resolve scope through `_resolve_code_quality_scope`; neither may diverge.
- **Framework boundary.** Changes belong in `skill/audit/` and `skill/code_review/` with tests in the repo's `tests/` and `skill/audit/tests/` trees; no production game/scene code is involved.

## Design decision and recommendation

Two approaches satisfy the brief; both are acceptable to the producer, so the implementer may choose:

1. **Absolutise the scope (recommended).** After filtering, map each in-scope relative path to `(project_root / path).resolve()` inside `_resolve_code_quality_scope` (that is, scope resolution away from *linting*, keeping `_filter_code_quality_scope`'s "returned unchanged" contract intact) and drop the cwd-relative `Path(path).exists()` fallback in `_filter_existing_paths`.
2. **Run the linter with `cwd=project_root`.** Thread a `cwd` through `run_code_quality` → `run_linters_for_project` → `run_ruff`/`_run_ruff_check` → runner. This is more invasive: `Runner` is `Callable[[Sequence[str]], CompletedProcess]` with no `cwd` parameter, so every layer (and every mocked runner in tests) would need to accept it.

**Recommended:** approach 1 — it is local to the audit's scope resolver, needs no runner signature change, keeps `_filter_code_quality_scope`'s pinned "unchanged and in order" behaviour, and still holds if re-scanning is ever invoked through a different runner. Whichever approach is taken, the `_filter_existing_paths` cwd fallback must go: it is the mechanism that lets a launch-checkout coincidence smuggle a non-existent code-root path into the scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the ghost paths in the observed run entered through the touched-files resolver (item `Key Files`) rather than through git, because git calls are already pinned with `git -C <code_root>`. The fix is designed to be correct for both sources.
- **Risk (medium):** removing the `Path(path).exists()` fallback changes `_filter_existing_paths` behaviour for any caller relying on launch-cwd resolution. Mitigation: keep the `project_root`-relative branch as the only relative branch and assert the same-repo path in tests; grep for other callers before changing the signature.
- **Risk (low):** absolute paths change finding `file` fields from relative to absolute in code-quality output for other consumers (`create_quality_epics.py`, the false-positive screen). Mitigation: check those consumers accept absolute paths and note it in the implementation.
- **Risk (low, scope creep):** while investigating, the same session noted that the audit F3 execution worktree does not link vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` — tracked separately; do **not** fold it into this item.
- **Failure mode to pin:** a scope that is non-empty but entirely absent from the code root must produce the empty-scope skip reason, not `E902` findings.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_code_quality_scope` (absolutise scope; both call sites), `_filter_existing_paths` (drop the cwd-relative fallback), and their docstrings.
- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `_run_ruff_check` / `run_ruff` path handling (and `cwd` threading if approach 2 is chosen). **Note:** the live package is the underscore form; `skill/code-review/` is a stale copy and is not imported.
- `skill/code_review/scripts/code_quality.py` — `run_code_quality(..., files=...)` pass-through docs (approach 2 only).
- `tests/test_code_quality_scoping.py` — extend with the cwd-independence / no-`E902` regression test.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_code_quality_scope.py` — extend with the scope-resolution regression test (`project_root` != process cwd).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — `--code-root` section (cross-repo launch requirement).

## Related work

- SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58 — scope the code-quality scan to changed files, read-only (introduced `files=`).
- SA-0MUI5ZYO6002W3KD — code-quality scope falls back to whole repo when the item is already committed (both call sites must resolve scope through the helper).
- SA-0MVPDTSRV0049KW2 — scope must exclude nested repositories and paths outside the project root (`_filter_code_quality_scope`).
- SA-0MSKI7QRM008OAS0 — a previous `E902` ghost finding (`skill/audit/skill/start-proxy`), i.e. the same symptom class, from the pre-scoping era.
- LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR — the `--code-root` / `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` option this bug is exercised by.
- WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 — the cross-repo item that surfaced the defect (ContextHub worklog; code in ContentCreator).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were needed: the seed brief (an audit report with logs, root-cause hypotheses and candidate acceptance criteria) already defined the problem, and verification against the codebase resolved the open choices (which module is live, where the cwd dependence actually sits, and which sources feed the scope).

Research record:

- Q: "Which code-quality module is live — `skill/code-review` or `skill/code_review`?" — Answer (repository inspection): the underscore package. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` imports `code_review.scripts.code_quality` / `code_review.scripts.linter_runner`; `skill/code-review/` is an unsymlinked stale copy whose `run_code_quality` lacks the `files` parameter. Source: `grep` over `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and both package copies.
- Q: "Is the git-derived scope also cwd-dependent?" — Answer (repository inspection): no. `_phase_gate` wraps the runner with `_cwd_aware_runner(git_root, runner)`, which prepends `git -C <code_root>` whenever the code root differs from the launch root. Source: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_cwd_aware_runner`.
- Q: "Where exactly can a launch-cwd path enter the scope?" — Answer (repository inspection): `_filter_existing_paths` keeps a relative path via `Path(path).exists()`, a stat against the process cwd; and `_run_ruff_check` passes the (relative) scope verbatim to `runner(cmd)` with no `cwd`. Source: `audit_runner.py` line ~7596, `linter_runner.py::_run_ruff_check`.
- **Recommended (advisory, producer may choose either):** absolutise the scope against `project_root` in `_resolve_code_quality_scope` — see *Design decision and recommendation*.

# Audit F3 execution worktree does not link vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` → spurious test failures and self-blocking triage children

**Discovered from:** WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 (Create a podcast for standups), `/skill:audit` run on 2026-11-21. Companion defect: the cross-repo `--code-root` code-quality scope bug (separate work item).

## Problem statement

The audit's default-on F3 suite execution builds a fresh execution worktree (`<repo>/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-<id>`, and a pinned worktree in the two-stage merge-gate path) and symlinks the **shared root `node_modules`** — but it does not provide the **vendored** dependency trees under `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`. Suites that exercise vendored extensions therefore fail inside the audit worktree while passing in the normal checkout.

Observed in the audit of WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 (ContentCreator suite, HEAD `d250032d4cea1f6a14b57459751eebdce1245acd`):

```
E  AssertionError: The vendored wiki extension is unavailable, so the rebuild cannot run:
   Cannot find package 'mdast-util-from-markdown' imported from
   /home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8/.pi/packages/pi-llm-wiki-manual/...
```

The package **is** present in the normal checkout (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/.pi/packages/pi-llm-wiki-manual/node_modules/mdast-util-from-markdown`), so the failure is an artefact of the audit worktree, not of the audited code. Three tests in `tests/test_rebuild_wiki_meta.py` failed this way.

## Consequence (why this is high priority)

1. The failures were correctly classified `unit`/`unrelated` and **excused** under the permissive test-failure mode — but they are still triaged, and triage created a **high-priority `test-failure` child parented to the audited epic** (`WL-0MWQXIR2J0001E1A`).
2. That child's own AC ("the test passes against the latest `dev`") is `unmet`, so the parent's audit verdict became **`Ready to close: No`** and the item was flagged `needsProducerReview` — an otherwise fully-complete epic blocked by a dependency artefact of the audit harness itself.
3. The producer had to review and delete the child as spurious before the item could be re-audited.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The audit F3 execution worktree (single-stage and the two-stage pinned/merge-gate variant) provides **every** vendored dependency tree the suite needs — e.g. initialise submodules, then link or bootstrap both the root `node_modules` **and** each `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` (or run the project's own bootstrap/install step).
- [ ] A repo whose suite depends on a vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` yields the **same** suite verdict in the audit execution worktree as in the normal checkout at the same commit.
- [ ] Suite failures whose evidence is a missing/absent dependency inside the audit worktree are classified as **infrastructure**, not product failures: they never create `test-failure` work items and never leave the audited item blocked by an auto-created child.
- [ ] A regression test pins the worktree preparation (or the infra-failure classification) without requiring a real suite run.
- [ ] `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` records the worktree dependency provisioning contract next to the existing `node_modules` symlink conventions.

## Impact

Audits stop failing work that is actually finished: vendored-dependency tests behave identically in the audit worktree and the real checkout, so no spurious high-priority test-failure child is created and producers are not asked to review and delete phantom blockers.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — F3 execution-worktree creation / `node_modules` symlink path, and the test-failure triage hand-off.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — suite execution in a supplied worktree (`cwd=`), triage classification of failures.
- `skill/triage/` — the `test-failure` item creation path (evidence used to decide whether a failure is infrastructure).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — worktree provision / symlink conventions.

## Evidence / related

# Provision vendored `node_modules` in audit worktrees

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

## Problem

The audit creates two throwaway worktrees — the F3 **execution** worktree
(`<host>/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-<id>`, `_create_execution_worktree`) and the
merge-gate **integration** worktree (`audit-merge-<id>`, `_integrate_into_dev`).
Both initialise git submodules and symlink the **root** `node_modules` only. A repo
that vendors a pi package under `.pi/packages/<pkg>/` with its own gitignored
`node_modules` therefore has an unresolvable dependency graph inside the worktree
while the populated checkout resolves it fine (observed: ContentCreator
`tests/test_rebuild_wiki_meta.py`, `Cannot find package 'mdast-util-from-markdown'`).

`implement.py` already solves this for implement worktrees
(`_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`). The audit has no equivalent, and there
must be **one** provisioner, not a second copy.

## Scope

- Promote the nested-`node_modules` discovery + symlink logic into a shared module.
- Call it from both audit worktree creation sites, after submodule initialisation
  and before the build/suite runs.
- Emit evidence lines so a reviewer can see what was provisioned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC1 — The audit F3 execution worktree (single-stage and the two-stage pinned/merge-gate variant) provides **every** vendored dependency tree the suite needs — e.g. initialise submodules, then link or bootstrap both the root `node_modules` **and** each `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` (or run the project's own bootstrap/install step).
- [ ] One shared provisioner (`skill/shared/worktree_deps.py`) discovers nested `node_modules` directories under a checkout root and symlinks each into the worktree, never overwriting an existing entry and never fabricating a package directory the worktree lacks.
- [ ] `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` keeps `_iter_nested_node_modules` / `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` as delegating wrappers, so its existing call sites and patched tests are unchanged.
- [ ] Both `_create_execution_worktree` (F3 execution worktree) and `_integrate_into_dev` (merge-gate worktree) provision nested `node_modules` after `_ensure_worktree_submodules` and before the build/suite, appending greppable evidence (`nested node_modules provisioned: <n> (<paths>)`, or a best-effort failure note).
- [ ] Provisioning is best-effort: a failure records evidence and never aborts the audit or fails the merge gate.
- [ ] Unit tests in `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` cover discovery pruning (`.git`/`.worklog`/`node_modules` never descended, symlinked dirs never followed, root `node_modules` excluded), symlink creation, no-overwrite, missing-parent skip, and per-candidate failure tolerance — with no suite execution.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Move `_NESTED_NODE_MODULES_PRUNE_DIRS`, `_iter_nested_node_modules` and `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` into `skill/shared/worktree_deps.py` (public names `iter_nested_node_modules`, `ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`).
2. Re-export them from `implement.py` as thin wrappers preserving the current return types and log lines.
3. Add `_provision_worktree_dependencies(worktree_path, host_root) -> list[str]` in `audit_runner.py`: the existing root `node_modules` symlink plus the nested symlinks, returning evidence lines.
4. Call it from `_create_execution_worktree` (after submodules, replacing the inline symlink block) and from `_integrate_into_dev` (same point in the integration sequence).
5. Add `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` — written red-first.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/worktree_deps.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` (existing merge-gate coverage to extend)

## Constraints

- Fail-open, mirroring `_ensure_worktree_submodules`: never a new hard dependency of the audit.
- Symlinks only: never copy, never install, never invoke a package manager inside a worktree (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B convention).
- Preserve the ordering hazard fix: submodules → dependency provisioning → build/suite (SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ).
- Cross-repo `--code-root` hosting of the merge-gate worktree is **out of scope** (execution-worktree hosting was SA-0MWO59J9T002IQ63); this slice provisions from the root each site already uses.

## Impact

Suites in the audit's throwaway worktrees resolve the same dependency graph as the real checkout, so vendored-package tests stop failing for environmental reasons.

# Classify audit-worktree dependency failures as infrastructure

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

## Problem

`_run_tests_via_test_skill` triages every parsed failure **before** the red-suite
mode evaluation runs, so a failure caused by the audit worktree's own missing
dependency still mints a critical `test-failure` child on the audited item
(WL-0MWQXIR2J0001E1A in the observed incident). The consequence: a complete epic
reads "Ready to close: No" and needs producer review to delete a phantom blocker.

A suppression contract already exists for verdicts that must never mint an item —
`detect_phantom` / `PHANTOM_NOTICE_CODES` for `state_changed_during_run`
(WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET). This slice adds the infrastructure case alongside it.

## Scope

- Evidence-based detector: a module-resolution failure whose importer path resolves
  inside the audit execution worktree **and** whose named dependency exists in the
  populated checkout.
- Audit runner: suppress those failures from triage (before any `wl` mutation) and
  report them.
- Triage helper: honour an explicit infrastructure signal so no caller can mint an
  item from it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC3 — Suite failures whose evidence is a missing/absent dependency inside the audit worktree are classified as **infrastructure**, not product failures: they never create `test-failure` work items and never leave the audited item blocked by an auto-created child.
- [ ] Detection is conservative and evidence-based: a missing-module/package failure is infrastructure only when the failing importer path resolves inside the audit execution worktree AND the named dependency is present in the populated checkout; a genuinely missing product dependency stays a product failure.
- [ ] The audit runner skips triage for infrastructure failures before any `wl` mutation (no `check_or_create` call, no dependency wiring) and records them in a `suppressed_infrastructure` result key plus the run summary line and gate evidence.
- [ ] `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` suppresses on the explicit signal (`notice_code: missing_dependency_in_worktree` or `infrastructure: true`) exactly as it does for phantoms, returning `suppressed: true` without a lookup or creation.
- [ ] Infrastructure failures never upgrade an execution-dependent AC to `met`: no green evidence means the AC stays `partial` (the runner's fail-closed evidence invariant is preserved).
- [ ] Unit tests pin detection positives and negatives plus both suppression paths (audit runner and triage helper) without executing a suite.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `skill/shared/test_infra.py`: `INFRA_NOTICE_CODE`, `detect_missing_dependency(text)` (Node `Cannot find module/package`, `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, Python `ModuleNotFoundError`, TS2307) and `classify_infrastructure_failure(failure, *, worktree_root, main_checkout_root)` returning `None` unless environment causality is proven.
2. `audit_runner.py`: partition `failures` before the triage loop so only product failures reach `check_or_create`; add `suppressed_infrastructure` to the returned dict and the `Test skill run completed:` summary line; surface the count in the evidence block.
3. `triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`: `detect_infrastructure(payload)` checked after `detect_phantom`, returning the same suppressed shape (no lookup, no creation, no dependency edge).
4. Tests: `skill/shared/tests/test_test_infra.py`, `skill/triage/tests/test_check_or_create_infrastructure.py`, and an audit-runner test asserting zero triage calls for an infrastructure failure record.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/test_infra.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_test_infra.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`
- `skill/triage/tests/test_check_or_create_infrastructure.py` (new)

## Constraints

- No inferred similarity: suppression fires only on evidence proving environment causality, so a genuine failure on a stable checkout is never swallowed.
- Never suppress a failure whose evidence does not name a missing module/package.
- Do not widen this into "excuse every unrelated failure": that ordering question is separate and out of scope.

## Impact

A missing vendored dependency inside the audit worktree can no longer create a phantom high-priority `test-failure` blocker on the audited item.

# Problem

A driven child session wrote outside its worktree (a dirty file in the main checkout) and neither `implement.py finish` nor the parent/drive placement guard detected it. The guard returned None because the child's worktree held commits — the three-condition gate assumes any main-checkout dirt is "pre-existing/unrelated" when the worktree is dirty, and never inspects the main checkout in that case.

# Evidence (epic VC-0MWNE567Z004NEX9, 2026-11-22T01:00Z)

- Driven child VC-0MWNNCB0S002TOM4 (target-duration slice) left `tests/helpers/fake-tools.ts` modified (+38 lines adding a `clipDurations` fake-ffprobe option) in the main checkout `/home/rgardler/projects/video_compiler`.
- The change is not on `dev`: the committed slice (9553294) uses the injected probe runner instead, so the main-checkout edit was an abandoned attempt written via an absolute path.
- `implement.py finish` for that child pushed successfully; no "changes outside the worktree" refusal was raised.

# Suspected cause

`_child_main_checkout_violation()` at line ~20734 in `implement.py` applies three conditions:

1. child is non-terminal
2. a foreign surface holds changes (main checkout dirty, or sibling dirty)
3. the child's worktree holds NO changes

When condition 3 fails (worktree has dirty files or commits ahead), the guard returns `None` immediately — it never inspects the main checkout. The logic assumes all main-checkout dirt is pre-existing/unrelated, but misses the case where the child wrote SOMETHING in both places.

# Users

- The agent implementing the child work item: the guard should refuse finish so the agent knows to move the edit into the worktree.
- The operator driving the epic: the parent/drive should fail closed, not silently let a foreign write through.

# Acceptance Criteria

- A driven child that leaves the main checkout dirty at a path inside the repo fails its `finish` with a placement-violation refusal, naming the offending paths.
- The same violation is detected by `_child_main_checkout_violation` when called from `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` (the parent/drive placement guard).
- The violation occurs even when the child's worktree also has commits ahead of the parent branch (the current gap: condition 3 is treated as a complete exemption).
- Covered by a test: a fake child that writes an absolute path under the main checkout is refused at `finish` with a placement violation.
- The failure message tells the agent to move the edit into the worktree and explains the rule (work must be inside the worktree, not in `cwd` alone).
- Pre-existing, unrelated dirt in the main checkout (unattributed to the child) is still handled correctly — the fix must not regress the existing exemption for ambient dirt when the worktree is the only change surface.
- Validation: the new behaviour is demonstrated by tests that fail before the fix and pass after it (guard-level and finish-gate level).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Impact

Users can no longer have work silently left in the main checkout when implementing a child task, preventing repo pollution and cross-contamination between concurrent work items.

# Constraints

- Do not change the existing exemption for ambient dirt when the worktree is the only change surface (condition 3's original intent: "pre-existing dirt does not block a legitimate finish when the work lives in the worktree").
- The fix must be compatible with the upcoming session-baseline system (SA-0MWM88CIH0026QXI / SA-0MWM88J2D001HFMS) — ideally, the guard's logic should be structured so that a baseline-aware comparison can be layered on top without reworking the entire function.

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_worktree_placement_violation`, `phase_parent`, `phase_finish`, `phase_drive`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — guard-level unit tests
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` — finish gate tests

- SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM — Enforce and document that driven child sessions must work inside their worktree (parent epic, completed)
- SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I — Sibling worktree stray write (related incident, AC3 in test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py)

- SA-0MWM88J2D001HFMS — Session-baseline lifecycle across start/parent/drive (blocked, sibling of the above)

# Risks & Assumptions

- Risk: The guard is conservative by design to avoid false positives on ambient dirt. Adding detection for "worktree dirty + main-checkout dirty" could trigger on legitimate concurrent development (e.g., the operator has uncommitted work in the main checkout). Mitigation: the guard already has the "worktree has NO changes" exemption; the fix tightens this only when the worktree IS dirty but the main checkout is also dirty — the violation message names the specific paths so the agent can judge.
- Risk: This fix must not break the upcoming session-baseline system (SA-0MWM88CIH0026QXI). The baseline system introduces a time dimension; this fix is orthogonal (it's a logic gap, not a false-positive issue).
- Assumption: The test harness can simulate a driven child with both a dirty main checkout and committed work in the worktree, using real git sandboxes (per the convention in test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py).

- Q: Should the guard detect writes to the main checkout even when the worktree has commits? — Answer: Yes. The current logic assumes any main-checkout dirt is pre-existing when the worktree is dirty, but a child that wrote in both places (abandoned a main-checkout edit, then committed work in the worktree) must be caught.
- Q: Does this interact with the session-baseline work (SA-0MWM88CIH0026QXI)? — Answer: No. That work addresses a different gap — distinguishing pre-existing from new dirt using timestamps. This gap is a logic omission — the main checkout is never checked when the worktree is dirty. Both fixes are orthogonal.
